text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The new Bulgarian president Petar Stoyanov took over as head of state and army's commander-in-chief at an official ceremony in Sofia.

-- Bulgaria's outgoing Prime minister Zhan Videnov criticised the initiative of the new Socialist party leader Georgi Parvanov to appologise to all Bulgarians who were mislead by the ruling Socialists. @

The government made no mistakes, political tension rose because the outgoing president Zhelyu Zhelev has delayed handing a mandate for formation of a new government to the Socialist party, Videnov was quoted as saying.

-- A possible interim government could continue funding talks with international lenders but no loan agreements could be expected, because there would be no parliament to approve the agreements, Bulgaria's outgoing Finance Minister Dimitar Kostov said.
-- The Bulgarian Socialist Party (BSP) executive bureau approved organisation of street rallies accross the country to support the BSP attempt to form a new government.
-- Monthly inflation for January is expected at 40-50 percent, a Bulgarian Academy of Sciences senior official said.
-- Bulgaria's State Fund for Reconstruction and Development has transfered $135 million to the Finance ministry to secure payment of Brady bond coupon due in January, the Finance ministry said.

-- Bulgaria expects to finalise the sale of a 25 percent stake in the Bulgarian Telecommunications Company by June and some $1 billion from the sell-off are expected in July or in August, outgoing deputy prime minister Roumen Gechev said.

-- Bulgarian drama students staged a symbolic burial for the ruling Socialist Party (BSP) in front of the mausoleum of the communist hero Georgi Dimitrov in central Sofia as a protest against the BSP attempts to form a new government.
-- Bulgaria's monopolist cigarette maker Bulgartabak holding said it had exported some 42,000 tonnes of cigarettes last year. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
